title: Persona → Pain Points → Messaging Matrix (Regulated Workloads ABM) — v1
body:
Working note (PMM + Security alignment):
- This matrix is the “source of truth” for what we can say externally during the regulated workloads ABM pilot.
- Approved language is intentionally specific + qualify/limit statements. Do not improvise compliance claims in outbound.
- Evidence pack sharing: only via approved process (NDA as needed). Do not attach SOC 2 / reports to cold email.
- If a prospect asks for something not covered here, route to: Naomi Feldman / Olga Petrov (GRC) + Dr. Aisha Rahman (exec).

Last review checkpoint:
- 2025-05-04 messaging review edits incorporated (see Gmail thread: soojin_lee/20250504-messaging-review-regulated-workloads)
- 2025-05-21 added audit log export clarification based on NorthBridge + Regal Wealth questions

How to use this sheet:
1) Pick persona row → copy “Approved language” into outreach / landing page sections.
2) Pair with a single asset + a single CTA (do not overload).
3) Keep the claim + proof point + asset consistent (ex: “audit logs available” → link Security FAQ section + offer evidence index).

=====================================================================
TAB: FINANCIAL SERVICES (FinServ)
=====================================================================
Columns:
Persona | Buying role | Primary pains (what they say) | Hidden concerns (what they mean) | Triggers/intent signals | Redwood fit (pillar) | Proof points to use | Best asset(s) | Recommended CTA | Discovery questions | Approved language (safe) | DO NOT SAY (risky / non-approved)

CISO / Head of Security | Economic + risk owner (blocker/approver) | “We can’t send customer data to a public API.” “We need auditability + controls.” | Vendor risk + board accountability; wants to avoid ‘shadow AI’ while enabling speed | Security questionnaire request, SOC2 request, “VPC / on-prem required”, “data residency” | Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) + Dedicated; audit logs; encryption + key management integration options | Security FAQ; evidence pack index; reference architecture overview; ability to isolate environment | Regulated Workloads Security FAQ; Evidence Pack Index; Regulated ABM deck (security slides) | 30-min security review call w/ Security + SE | “What workloads are in scope (PHI/PCI/PII)?” “What is your minimum control set (SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs)?” “Do you require customer-managed keys?” | “Redwood supports private deployment options (VPC and on-prem) designed for regulated environments.” “We can share our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and walk through scope.” “We provide audit logging for key administrative and inference events, with export options for SIEM workflows.” | “We are HIPAA compliant / PCI certified.” “We guarantee you will pass your audit.” “Zero data retention in all cases.” “We are compliant with every regulation.”

GRC / Vendor Risk Manager | Process gatekeeper | “Your security answers are too vague.” “We need evidence.” | Wants fast, standardized responses; fears exception process | Security questionnaire in first 2 weeks, evidence pack request | Evidence pack process; standardized answers; fast turnaround | Prior completed questionnaires (redacted); SOC2 process; policy statements on retention/residency | Security FAQ; Evidence Pack Index; sample audit log fields (sanitized) | “Send evidence pack index + schedule 45-min vendor risk review” | “Do you have a preferred questionnaire format (SIG / CAIQ)?” “What evidence is required vs optional?” | “We have a sales-ready security FAQ and an evidence pack index to streamline review; we can provide artifacts through an NDA process.” “We can commit to a response SLA for security questionnaires during evaluation.” | “We’ll send all security documents over email today.” “Everything is available publicly.”

Platform Engineering Lead (Cloud / Infra) | Technical evaluator + strong influencer | “Latency is unpredictable.” “We can’t get stable throughput.” “We need deployment flexibility.” | Doesn’t want to build/operate full inference stack; needs reliability | Benchmark downloads; “dedicated capacity”; “multi-region”; mention of autoscaling | Dedicated capacity; Private deployment; predictable throughput + SLOs; routing/fallback | Benchmark results template; reference architecture; console screenshots; pilot plan | Regulated ABM deck (arch + performance); one-pager (FinServ) | “Run a 2-week benchmark + architecture validation (SE-led)” | “What are your p95 latency + throughput targets?” “Traffic shape (streaming vs batch)?” “Do you need single-tenant GPUs?” | “Redwood Dedicated provides reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput, with operational tooling (routing, fallbacks, dashboards) to keep SLOs stable.” “We can validate latency/throughput with a scoped pilot using your request mix.” | “We’re always faster than X.” “We guarantee exact latency numbers without running your workload.”

ML Engineering / Applied ML Lead | Technical evaluator | “Quality regresses when we optimize for cost.” “We need controllable rollouts.” | Fear of model/quantization changes impacting accuracy; wants evals + guardrails | Requests for A/B tests; asks about quantization, batching, caching | Optimize toolkit + rollouts; version pinning; canary/fallback | Console rollouts overview; eval harness guidance; quality monitoring approach | ABM deck (rollouts + economics); pilot plan outline | “Bring 20–50 prompts / golden set; we’ll set up evaluation + canary” | “How do you measure quality today?” “Tolerance for quantization?” “Do you need model pinning + rollback?” | “You can pin model versions and roll out changes with canary/fallback policies, so performance optimizations don’t require blind quality risk.” | “We’ll never change anything.” “Quality will always be identical.”

Fraud / Risk Ops (FinServ line-of-business) | Budget influencer; use-case champion | “Fraud ops is slow.” “We need better triage and explanations.” | Wants measurable impact; fears compliance + audit trail gaps | Fraud tooling RFP; asks about human-in-the-loop + audit | Low-latency + auditability; dedicated throughput; logging | Example use cases: fraud case summarization; agent assist; audit logging narrative | FinServ one-pager; webinar invite | “30-min use-case discovery + success metrics mapping” | “What’s the workflow today?” “Where do analysts spend time?” “What needs to be logged for audit?” | “We support patterns for human-in-the-loop workflows with auditability and controlled retention options appropriate for regulated environments.” | “Fully autonomous fraud decisions.” “Replace analysts.”

Procurement | Commercial gatekeeper | “This doesn’t fit our vendor model.” “Need clarity on pricing + terms.” | Wants predictability; avoids open-ended usage bills | Mentions marketplace, private offer, DPA/SLA | Dedicated/Private constructs; predictable commits; marketplace path | Packaging notes (internal); marketplace process overview | “Commercial + procurement intro call (30 min)” | “Do you prefer annual commit vs monthly?” “Marketplace required?” “DPA/SLA requirements?” | “We offer Dedicated and Private commercial constructs that align with reserved capacity and enterprise support needs; we can also pursue AWS Marketplace private offers where applicable.” | “We can match any price.” “Standard terms are non-negotiable.”

Legal (Privacy / Data) | Contract + policy approver | “Data processing terms and retention are unclear.” | Liability + residency issues; data boundaries | DPA redlines; data residency questions | Clear DPA posture; retention/residency options; audit logs | DPA template (via Legal); retention policy statements | “Legal + security working session (45 min)” | “Do you require specific regions?” “Retention default expectations?” “Subprocessor requirements?” | “We can support data residency requirements via deployment options and contractual commitments, subject to agreed regions and configuration.” “We can document retention options and audit logging behavior for your review.” | “We don’t store anything ever.” “Data never leaves your country in any case.”

=====================================================================
TAB: HEALTHCARE / PHI-ADJACENT
=====================================================================
Columns:
Persona | Buying role | Primary pains | Hidden concerns | Triggers/intent signals | Redwood fit (pillar) | Proof points to use | Best asset(s) | Recommended CTA | Discovery questions | Approved language (safe) | DO NOT SAY (risky / non-approved)

CIO / VP IT (Health system) | Executive sponsor + prioritization | “We need to modernize patient/member experience without creating risk.” | Reputational risk; vendor sprawl; needs cross-team alignment | “PHI”, “BAA”, “on-prem”, “VPC only”, “retention policy” | Private deployments; governance; predictable ops | Architecture options; security posture overview; pilot plan that avoids PHI where possible | Healthcare one-pager; webinar outline; security FAQ | “Exec + security + app team discovery (45 min)” | “What’s in scope (PHI vs de-identified)?” “Where does the data live today?” “Any mandated vendors/tools?” | “We support private deployment patterns (VPC/on-prem) that can be aligned with your data handling policies, including audit logging and access controls.” | “HIPAA certified.” “HIPAA compliant out of the box.”

Security Officer / HIPAA Security (or equivalent) | Risk owner | “We need controls and audit trails for access + changes.” | Wants enforcement + visibility; skeptical of AI vendors | Security questionnaire; requests for logging, RBAC, SSO | Audit logs; RBAC/SSO/SAML; encryption; evidence pack | Security FAQ specifics; audit log field examples (sanitized) | Security FAQ; Evidence Pack Index | “Security review + evidence pack request kickoff” | “Who needs access (admins vs users)?” “Audit log retention/export needs?” “SSO requirements?” | “We support SSO (SAML) and role-based access controls, and we can provide audit logs for key events with export options to support compliance workflows.” | “We log everything about patient data.” “We provide immutable logs that meet every requirement by default.”

Clinical Informatics / Clinical Ops | Champion (use-case + adoption) | “Clinicians are burnt out.” “Documentation burden is too high.” | Needs safety + explainability; fear of hallucinations | Interest in summarization/coding assistance; asks about guardrails | Controlled rollouts; quality monitoring; private deployment to align policy | Pilot plan emphasizing evaluation + guardrails; structured output | Healthcare one-pager; pilot plan template | “2-week scoped pilot with eval set + approval workflow” | “What outputs must be verified?” “What’s acceptable error rate?” “Any prohibited data types?” | “We recommend a scoped evaluation with agreed success metrics and guardrails (e.g., human review, structured outputs) before broader rollout.” | “This will replace clinicians.” “Guaranteed accuracy.”

Revenue Cycle / Medical Billing Ops | Budget influencer | “Coding and claims workflows are slow/expensive.” | Wants ROI; cost predictability; batch workloads | Requests for batch processing; cost questions | Dedicated throughput; cost/performance controls; batching | Cost breakdown approach; batching/caching explanation | Healthcare one-pager; ABM deck (economics) | “Batch workload assessment + cost model review (30 min)” | “Batch size and SLA?” “Peak vs steady workloads?” “Do you require dedicated capacity?” | “We can optimize batch-style workloads using workload-aware batching and caching approaches, and validate cost/latency in a small pilot.” | “We’ll cut your costs by X% guaranteed.”

Data Privacy Officer | Policy approver | “We need clear retention and data handling boundaries.” | Concerned about downstream use, training, and residency | Data processing questions; retention/residency policy request | Private deployment; retention controls; documentation | Retention policy statements; DPA terms (through Legal) | Security FAQ + privacy section | “Privacy + security review (45 min)” | “Retention default expectations?” “Any restrictions on logging content?” | “We can document data handling boundaries and retention options for logs and content, and align configuration to your policies during evaluation.” | “We never retain anything in any form.”

Procurement / Vendor Management (Healthcare) | Commercial gatekeeper | “We need predictable spend and clear implementation plan.” | Worried about hidden integration/support costs | Mentions implementation timeline, support tiers | Dedicated/Private constructs; support tiers | Pilot plan with roles/responsibilities; support overview | Pilot plan outline; ABM deck (implementation) | “Commercial + implementation scoping call” | “Who owns implementation internally?” “Support requirements?” | “We can provide a structured pilot plan with clear roles, success criteria, and options for enterprise support aligned to regulated deployments.” | “Implementation is always self-serve.”

=====================================================================
GLOBAL (applies to all verticals) — Approved Claims & Red Flags
=====================================================================
Approved claim patterns (use these templates):
- “Supports …” / “Can be configured to …” / “We can provide … under NDA” / “Subject to deployment mode and configuration …”
- “Private deployment options (VPC/on-prem) for regulated environments” (avoid implying a certification)
- “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA; we can walk through scope and controls”
- “Audit logging for key events; export options for customer tooling (SIEM) workflows”
- “SSO (SAML) + RBAC available; SCIM availability depends on plan/deployment (confirm before promising)”
- “Data residency options depend on region/deployment; confirm required region list early”

Do not say / red flags (route to Security/Legal):
- “HIPAA compliant / HIPAA certified / PCI certified / FedRAMP” (unless explicitly confirmed for a specific scope, which we are not claiming in this pilot)
- “Zero retention everywhere / we never store anything” (retention varies by configuration and logging requirements)
- “End-to-end encryption” (be precise: encryption in transit/at rest; key management options)
- “Immutable audit logs” (only say what’s true + documented)
- “Guaranteed pass audit / guaranteed latency/cost numbers”
- “We don’t use subprocessors” / “no third parties” (Legal must confirm)

Notes for outbound writers (Ben/Grace/Rohan):
- Keep first email to 2 pillars max: (1) deployment control for regulated + (2) predictable performance economics.
- CTA preference for regulated: “security review call” or “benchmark + architecture validation” (avoid generic “book a demo” unless persona is technical).

Open questions / to confirm before ‘final’:
- SCIM availability wording by deployment mode (pending: product confirmation)
- Audit log export formats + retention defaults (pending: ENG-22091 close-out + docs update)
- Healthcare wording: confirm we avoid any ‘HIPAA-ready’ phrasing in outbound (Security preference: avoid)
